answer: The juniper detector writes to zephyr, and lagoon shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 165 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 277 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 6 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
